_doc: Shared conformance fixture for the session-segment library format. mogwai-lab WRITES this shape (mogwai_lab::segments) and mogwai-data READS it (mogwai_data::segment); neither can depend on the other's type, because mogwai-lab depends on mogwai-data and never the reverse. Both crates parse THIS file in their own tests, so a format drift fails one side instead of leaving both green against a private idea of the shape. Hand-written, not cut from corpus: the numbers are shaped to exercise the contract, not to be realistic.

units.ret: nano-log-returns: round(ln(p / p_prev) * 1e9), against the previous trade in the same segment
units.open_gap_ret: nano-log-returns from the last real print BEFORE the window to this segment's first print, or null when no prior print existed
units.dt_ns: nanoseconds since the previous trade; dt_ns[0] is measured from the window start
units.side: DBN aggressor alphabet: B taker-buy, A taker-sell, N unsided
units.tick_size: decimal string, the instrument's price increment

rules: dt_ns, ret, size and side are PARALLEL arrays, all of length trade_count. Both readers refuse a library where they disagree.
ret[0] is always 0: the first trade of a segment is its own anchor, and its displacement from the previous session lives in open_gap_ret.
A segment carries NO absolute price. Absolute level is an integration constant the composer supplies, which is what lets any segment follow any other without a level discontinuity.
trade_count is never 0: an empty segment would advance the loop without advancing the tape.
version must equal the reader's SEGMENT_LIBRARY_VERSION; a mismatch is refused rather than interpreted.
